papers.title: Ordered Cu─Pd Intermetallic Alloy With Complementary Facets Enables Efficient Urea Electrosynthesis via Accelerated C─N
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT CO 2 and nitrate are widespread contaminants. Co‐electrolysis of them to produce urea enables eco‐friendly pollution treatment and agricultural support, while bare Cu suffers low selectivity, quick deactivation and dominant hydrogen evolution reaction competition. Herein, we synthesize long‐range ordered concave CuPd intermetallics (f‐CuPd) by liquid reduction and gradient annealing. Characterizations confirm annealing converts disordered face‐centered cubic d‐CuPd to ordered body‐centered cubic phase. Fully ordered f‐CuPd exposes complementary (211) and (001) facets with evenly mixed Cu and Pd without segregation. Its ordered atomic arrangement induces Pd to Cu charge transfer and restrains Cu surface oxidation. Electrochemical measurements reveal exceptional electrocatalytic activity toward urea synthesis, attaining a urea production rate of 74.78 mmol h −1 g cat −1 and steady catalytic activity throughout 28 h of uninterrupted electrolysis. In situ spectra track the reaction and prove the ordered structure adjusts interfacial water to generate active hydrogen and avoid competitive adsorption of CO 2 and nitrate intermediates. Density functional theory calculations uncover a unique synergistic effect between two crystal facets. The (211) facet drives efficient CO 2 activation to form * CO intermediates, while the adjacent (001) facet facilitates nitrate reduction and C─N coupling with substantially reduced kinetic barriers. Reaction intermediates migrate across distinct crystal facets, driving highly efficient urea formation.

papers.title: Medium‐Entropy Hydroxides Enable Bridge‐Bound NO Stabilization and Hydrogen Spillover for Nitrite‐to‐Ammonia Electroreduction
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Electroreduction of nitrite provides a route to couple aqueous nitrite remediation with ammonia synthesis, but high selectivity requires coordinated nitrite deoxygenation and surface‐hydrogen delivery. Here, we report ultrathin NiFeCoCu medium‐entropy layered double hydroxide (ME‐LDH) nanosheets that promote selective nitrite‐to‐ammonia conversion by coupling charge‐polarized bridge‐bound * NO stabilization with hydrogen‐spillover‐assisted hydrogenation. In neutral K 2 SO 4 electrolyte containing nitrite, the catalyst delivers NH 4 + Faradaic efficiencies above 90% from −0.5 to −0.9 V vs. the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), reaches a max i mum Faradaic efficiency of 99%, and achieves an NH 4 + yield rate of 7417 µg·h −1 ·cm −2 . Quasi‐in situ x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), in situ Fourier‐transform infrared (FT‐IR) spectroscopy, isotope‐resolved spectroscopy, differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), kinetic isotope effect (KIE) analysis, and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) collectively support dynamic charge redistribution, bridge‐bound * NO formation, and rapid generation and consumption of surface active hydrogen, consistent with hydrogen‐spillover‐assisted hydrogenation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further reveal the preferential stabilization of bridge‐bound * NO at multimetal sites and the thermodynamically unfavorable accumulation of isolated H on the fully hydroxylated surface, providing theoretical support for the proposed adsorption–hydrogen‐transfer pathway. These findings highlight adsorption‐spillover coupling as a promising design strategy for entropy‐engineered hydroxides in nitrogen‐cycle electrocatalysis.

papers.title: Electronic Coupling and Dual‐Spillover Effect in Co/Co7Fe3 Heterointerface for Boosting Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Conversion
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Rational design of dual‐site catalysts to decouple complex multi‐electron pathways is crucial for efficient electrocatalytic nitrate (NO 3 − ) reduction reaction (NO 3 RR). Here, we construct a Co/Co 7 Fe 3 heterojunction with strong electronic coupling that drives NO 3 RR efficiently via an unconventional [4+4] tandem mechanism. In this [4+4] pathway, the first 4‐electron step reduces NO 3 − to the *HNOH intermediate at the Fe sites. The second 4‐electron process involves the migration of *HNOH to adjacent Co sites, followed by a 4‐electron hydrogenation step. Experimental and theoretical investigations demonstrate that the interfacial electric field modulates the local water network, accelerating water dissociation and ensuring a robust proton supply via hydrogen spillover. Benefiting from well‐defined heterointerfaces, the adsorption energetics of key intermediates are favorably optimized, endowing Co/Co 7 Fe 3 with markedly boosted electrocatalytic activity for NO 3 RR through synergistic dual‐spillover effects, and enabling it to achieve a near‐unity Faradaic efficiency of 99.16% ± 0.3% and a remarkable NH 3 yield rate of 36.07 ± 0.52 mg h −1 cm −2 at −0.48 V versus RHE. Additionally, a rechargeable Zn‐nitrate battery featuring this material as the cathode delivers a peak power density of 18.15 mW cm −2 with excellent cycling stability. This study provides a novel paradigm for designing efficient tandem electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Proton‐Induced Perthionitrite‐Mediated Zinc Thiolate Persulfidation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The perthionitrite anion, SSNO − , has been proposed as a S 0 source for persulfidation of biological thiol and thiolate compounds. Here, SSNO − reacts with an iminopyridine‐supported zinc thiolate complex to form a perthiolate‐supported zinc perthionitrite complex, acting as both a ligand to zinc and as a sulfur source for persulfidation of the thiolate moiety. A related zinc thionitrite complex was also prepared, enabling comparison of zinc thionitrite and zinc thiolate persulfidation. In these compounds, the zinc‐bound SNO − ligand is selectively persulfidated over the zinc‐bound thiolate moiety upon addition of S 8 , cleanly forming SSNO − rather than the perthiolate. This work therefore demonstrates that direct S 0 transfer from SSNO − to thiolate anions is thermodynamically unfavorable and must instead be mediated by preceding SSNO − decomposition.

papers.title: Reversing Electrochemical Spongification by Asymmetric Breathing for 380‐hour Hydroxylamine Electrosynthesis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic nitrate‐to‐hydroxylamine (NH 2 OH) conversion offers a sustainable route for reactive nitrogen upcycling. Metallic bismuth (Bi) is intrinsically active for this reaction, yet undergoes severe structural degradation under continuous electrolysis—a failure mode we identify as electrochemical spongification, wherein the compact Bi framework cathodically relaxes into an electrically disconnected porous network. Herein, we report an “asymmetric electrochemical breathing” strategy that effectively decouples long‐term catalytic durability from structural failure. Using pulsed potentials between −1.36 and +1.24 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), BiOCl nanosheets serve as a dynamic template, delivering a high Faradaic efficiency of 71.7% and a yield rate of 4.29 mmol h −1 cm −2 , among the highest reported for NH 2 OH electrosynthesis. Experimental and theoretical insights reveal that BiOCl rapidly reduces in situ to dense metallic Bi to drive efficient nitrate reduction. Crucially, a brief anodic pulse reconstructs the framework before irreversible degradation occurs, enabling continuous structural rejuvenation for over 380 h. This dynamic reconstruction strategy successfully suppresses the Faradaic efficiency decay rate by two orders of magnitude, establishing a robust paradigm for stabilizing highly active yet metastable electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Breaking the Activity–Stability Trade-Off in Electrochemical NO2– Reduction to NH3 over a Robust Fe3C/CN Catalyst
papers.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrite reduction coupled with plasma nitrogen oxidation offers a promising route for ambient ammonia synthesis, yet simultaneously achieving high activity and stability remains challenging owing to high kinetic barriers and catalyst deactivation. Here, we develop a robust hybrid electrocatalyst for active and durable nitrite reduction to ammonia by leveraging Fe3C nanoparticles supported on nitrogen-doped carbon nanosheets (Fe3C/CN). As a benefit from strong interactions between Fe3C and CN, this hybrid catalyst delivers a high faradaic efficiency of 89.6% at −0.7 V versus a reversible hydrogen electrode (vs RHE) and a record ammonia yield rate of 16 956.5 mmol h–1 gcat–1 at −0.9 V vs RHE, along with no apparent performance decay over 1000 h of continuous electrolysis, underscoring its potential for sustainable electrochemical ammonia production. Mechanistic studies reveal that the synergistic effect between Fe3C nanoparticles and a nitrogen-doped carbon matrix enhances catalytic performance by optimizing reactant adsorption, water dissociation, and promoting reaction kinetics.

papers.title: Free‐Standing High‐Entropy Oxides for Efficient Electrocatalytic Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT A novel free‐standing high‐entropy oxides (HEOs) catalyst, i.e., zinc oxide nano‐array decorated with iron, cobalt, nickel, copper, and zinc oxides (ZnO‐HEOs), is proposed firstly. It exhibits outstanding electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 − RR) capacity in the neutral electrolyte, achieving a Faradaic efficiency of ∼99.42% with an ammonia yield of ∼34.09 mg cm −2 h −1 in a membrane electrode assembly under optimal conditions. Meanwhile, it delivers an open‐circuit potential of ∼1.55 V with a peak power density of ∼5.33 mW cm −2 in a zinc‐nitrate battery. The performance of ZnO‐HEOs surpasses that of HEOs powder counterparts and most previously reported catalysts or cathode materials, because the difference in electron work function between ZnO and HEOs triggers their interfacial synergistic effect. It facilitates the charge transfer from ZnO‐HEOs to key intermediates, thereby changing the rate‐determining step of ZnO and HEOs toward the electrocatalytic NO 3 − RR, and decreasing their energy barrier simultaneously. More importantly, the ZnO‐HEOs can also sustain exceptional stability in both electrochemical systems, due to the fact that the ZnO supports effectively stabilize the active sites of HEOs. This work not only offers a route for the rational design of efficient and stable self‐supporting HEOs, but also promotes their practical applications in energy‐ and environment‐related fields.

papers.title: Molecular Engineering of Hemicyanine Scaffold for Peroxynitrite‐Activated Chemiluminescence Imaging
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Chemiluminescence eliminates interference from real‐time excitation light, thereby maximizing the signal‐to‐noise ratio of imaging. However, the reported chemiluminescent scaffolds remain limited, and the development of novel and efficient chemiluminescent scaffolds is critical and urgent. Herein, we synthesized a series of peroxynitrite (ONOO − )‐activated chemiluminescent probes based on a hemicyanine scaffold through molecular engineering, and systematically investigated optical properties as well as their response mechanisms. Upon reaction with ONOO − , the vinylene units in the hemicyanine scaffold are oxidatively degraded, thereby emitting a chemiluminescent signal in the 400–650 nm wavelength range. Furthermore, under the defined conditions, it was found that the tissue penetration of ONOO − ‐activated chemiluminescence (up to 12 mm) is deeper than that of 660 nm‐activated afterglow luminescence and the fluorescence of hemicyanine scaffolds. In cell imaging, in addition to sensitive ONOO − response via chemiluminescence, it can also respond superiorly to ONOO − through well‐separated dual fluorescence channels. In conjunction with satisfactory biocompatibility, the probe showed favorable responsiveness and high sensitivity toward ONOO − levels in lipopolysaccharide‐induced inflammation induced. These findings provide solid and reliable experience for the discovery and construction of novel and versatile chemiluminescent scaffolds.

papers.title: Axial Cl‐Coordinated Porous FeCoZn Trimetallic Single‐Atom Catalysts: Breaking the Linear Scaling Relation for Superior Oxygen Reduction Reaction and Ultrastable Zinc‐Air Batteries
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as a research frontier in electrocatalysis. However, conventional SACs possess single metal active sites, which hardly break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of M–N 4 . To address this limitation, porous trimetallic single‐atom catalysts (TACs) is fabricated via ZIF‐8‐derived ion exchange and gas‐phase etching methods. The catalyst features Fe, Co, and Zn single atoms with a special M–N 4 configuration where the three metal atoms share one N ligand. And axial coordination structure exists between Zn and Cl atoms. It exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction activity and stability under acidic/alkaline conditions, with a half‐wave potential of 0.81 V/0.96 V and loss of 4 mV/8 mV after 30 000 cycles. Only 6.5% performance decay is observed after 2163 h of charge‐discharge cycling in zinc‐air batteries (ZABs). Physicochemical characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the trimetallic configuration breaks the geometric and electronic structural symmetry, optimizing the adsorption of intermediates during the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Axial coordination of Cl on Zn facilitates the bridge‐type adsorption of O 2 and breaks the linear scaling relationship. This work offers a novel strategy to break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of SACs and regulate reaction pathways.

papers.title: High‐Entropy Platinum‐Group Metal Phosphide Atomic Layers With Controlled Phosphorization for Electrocatalytic Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT High‐entropy phosphides (HEP), derived from high‐entropy alloys (HEA), combine multimetallic active sites with phosphorus‐induced structural and electronic modulation, yet remain difficult to construct at the atomic‐layer scale. Here, a two‐step phosphorization and epitaxial‐growth strategy is developed to synthesize Pd@PdP@HEP nanocrystals with surface‐confined PdPtIrRhRuP HEP atomic layers. This design is further supported by density functional theory (DFT) formation‐energy calculations, which indicate that P preferentially occupies surface and near‐surface sites. Controlled phosphorization of Pd cubic seeds enables systematic regulation of P incorporation, lattice expansion, and structural disorder, while subsequent multimetallic growth produces compositionally complex surface layers. Electron microscopy and synchrotron‐based X‐ray absorption spectroscopy confirm the formation of P‐enriched HEP atomic layers and reveal strong electronic coupling between P and neighboring metal atoms. The optimized Pd@PdP@HEP catalyst exhibits higher alkaline hydrogen‐evolution activity than commercial Pt/C and the unphosphorized Pd@HEA counterpart, while maintaining excellent durability. DFT calculations show that P‐induced surface reconstruction and charge redistribution downshift the d‐band center, bring the hydrogen adsorption free energy (ΔG H* ) closer to thermoneutrality, and shift the hydroxyl adsorption free energy (ΔG OH* ) toward more positive values. These effects create a balanced adsorption environment, contribute to enhanced alkaline hydrogen‐evolution kinetics, and provide an effective strategy for engineering nonmetal‐modified high‐entropy catalysts.

papers.title: Engineering Abundant Mesopores in FeNC Single‐Atom Catalysts via High‐Gravity for High‐Performance Oxygen Reduction Reaction
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The performance of FeNC single atom catalysts (SACs) is significantly influenced by the porous architecture of their N‐doped carbon substrates. Although the pore structure of FeNC SACs has been widely investigated from a chemical methodology perspective, the role of synthesis process engineering has received much less attention. To address this, high‐gravity technology is introduced during the precursor preparation stage to achieve intensive molecular mixing. This approach successfully yields FeNC SACs with a well‐defined hierarchical micro‐mesoporous structure. The resulting catalyst exhibits a narrower mesopore size distribution (4–6 nm), a higher specific surface area (800.3 m 2 ·g −1 ), and a more positive half‐wave potential (0.899 V) for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) compared to a reference sample produced in a conventional stirred tank reactor. Density functional theory (DFT) analysis further indicates that the abundant mesopores induce carbon defects, thereby enhancing the intrinsic ORR activity. Moreover, when integrated into a zinc‐air battery and an anion‐exchange membrane fuel cell, the catalyst delivers high peak power densities of 259.5 and 860 mW·cm −2 , respectively, highlighting its potential for practical applications.

papers.title: Stabilizing Cobalt Sites with d10-Configured p-Block Cations for Iridium-Free Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) requires anode catalysts that sustain acidic oxygen evolution in practical stacks with minimal noble-metal content. Cobalt spinel oxides are cost-attractive but dissolve rapidly in acid as cobalt sites over-oxidize under anodic bias. Here we show that incorporation of d10-configured p-block cations (Sb, Ge, In, and Ga) into Co3O4 stabilizes cobalt sites by promoting robust heterometallic Co–O–M interactions. Density functional theory predicts dopant-driven charge redistribution that suppresses over-oxidation of octahedral Co while maintaining favorable binding of oxygen intermediates. Operando Co K-edge X-ray absorption and time-resolved dissolution measurements confirm reduced oxidation-state dynamics and cobalt loss, whereas a d-block d10 control (Zn) shows no such stabilization. In a PEMWE single cell at 80 °C, Sb/Co3O4 reaches >3500 mA cm–2 at 2.0 V and operates for >1000 h at 250 mA cm–2. This work establishes p-block d10 incorporation as a general route to iridium-free PEMWE anodes.

papers.title: In Situ X-ray Spectroscopic Identification and Kinetic Control of Highly Hybridized Co(IV) States in Cobalt Oxide Amorphous Catalysts
papers.abstract: Abstract Valence dynamics of transition metals are central to oxygen evolution reaction (OER) mechanisms, yet in situ spectroscopic studies capturing these dynamics within amorphous catalysts remain limited. Here, we present in situ X-ray spectroscopy of amorphous catalysts, where CoBi exhibits higher OER performance compared to CoPi. While our data shows successive valence changes toward high-valent states in both catalysts, distinct initial electro-structural states dictate the intermediate evolution. Co(III) dominates in both catalysts at open-circuit potential, yet the Co(III)–O–Co(III) bridge structure observed in CoBi is absent in CoPi. Under active OER, Co(IV) species are identified as distinguishable spectral intensities; these are assigned to highly hybridized low-spin (LS) Co(IV) with reduced electron–electron repulsion, as validated by resonant inelastic X-ray spectroscopy (RIXS) analysis of Li0.75CoO2. Density functional theory supports the conversion from tetrahedral (Td) Co(II) to octahedral (Oh) Co(III) and suggests that factors other than thermodynamic pathways are likely responsible for the performance gap. The lower formal oxidation, larger Co–O length, smaller Co–O–Co angle, prominent pre-edge dipole character and absent oxo-bridging in CoPi suggest a kinetically inefficient Co(IV) state. These findings demonstrate that the initial electro-structure strongly influences the formation of productive high-valent active species and the resulting OER activity.

papers.title: Disrupting Interfacial Hydrogen-Bonding Networks via Dynamic Reconstruction Strategy for Enhanced CO2-to-C2+ Electrocatalysis
papers.abstract: Abstract The morphology and microenvironment of ion-conducting polymers (ionomers) on the catalyst electrode surface critically govern the CO2 electrocatalytic performance. Herein, we report a dual-reconstruction strategy that synergistically tailors the surface structure of the Nafion ionomer using positively charged molecules and solvent effect. By combining a low-dielectric-constant solvent (isopropanol) with arginine cations, the optimized electrode achieves an 83.6% Faradaic efficiency for multicarbon (C2+) products at a high current density of –500 mA cm–2 in 1 M KOH. Based on experimental characterization and MD simulations, we propose a structural model in which the Nafion side chains are oriented away from both the catalyst surface and the electrolyte phase. In situ spectroscopic analyses, theoretical calculation, and experimental evidence suggest that this structural reorganization disrupts the interfacial hydrogen-bonding network, suppresses the competing hydrogen evolution reaction, improves effective gaseous CO2 accessibility, and facilitates C–C coupling along an energetically favorable *OC–COH pathway. This work provides valuable insights into microenvironment engineering of ionomer–catalyst interfaces for efficient CO2 electrolysis.

papers.title: In-Situ Visualization of Thermal Transformation Pathways in Leaf-Shaped Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework Derived Nanocarbon
papers.abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are versatile precursors for nanostructured, heteroatom-doped carbons. However, understanding the spatiotemporally resolved mechanisms that govern crystalline-to-amorphous framework collapse, diffusion-mediated reorganization of transient intermediates, and the subsequent formation of graphitic carbon remains challenging. Here, we elucidate the transformation of the 2D leaf-shaped zeolitic imidazolate framework ZIF-L into Zn-dispersed N-doped carbon using a combination of in situ transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD). These measurements directly capture the sequential collapse of the layered MOF framework and the associated morphological evolution under controlled heating, decoupled from beam-induced effects during electron microscopy. Complementary ex-situ pyrolysis (700–1100 °C), together with high-resolution TEM, synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function (X-PDF) analysis, and electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS), reveals the diffusion of Zn-containing species, ligand decomposition, and progressive graphitization within the amorphous matrix. We identify temperature-dependent stages involving ligand breakdown, migration of Zn–Nx species, followed by Zn loss, and ultimately forming porous N-doped carbon at 1000 °C that exhibits the strongest electrochemical response within this series. These findings establish temperature-dependent structure–property relationships that enable the thermal engineering of MOF-derived ORR catalysts.

papers.title: Atomically Dispersed Fe–Mo Catalytic Pairs Enable Two‐Electron Li2C2O4 Pathway for Reversible Li–CO2 Batteries
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐carbon dioxide (Li–CO 2 ) batteries present a promising strategy for coupling high‐energy storage with CO 2 utilization, yet their development is impeded by sluggish kinetics and severe polarization associated with insulating discharge products. Achieving selective and reversible two‐electron conversion toward Li 2 C 2 O 4 remains a critical challenge for improving energy efficiency and cycling stability. Herein, we report electronically asymmetric dual‐atom Fe–N–Mo catalytic pairs anchored on a highly conjugated N‐doped carbon (NC) framework, forming Fe 1 ‐Mo 1 integrated catalytic pairs (Fe 1 ‐Mo 1 /ICPs) to promote a reversible two‐electron Li 2 C 2 O 4 conversion pathway. The πconjugated highly conjugated N‐doped carbon framework stabilizes atomically dispersed Fe and Mo sites while enhancing inter‐site electronic coupling. Within the proposed heteronuclear Fe–N–Mo configuration, intrinsic electronic asymmetry generates electrophilic Fe and nucleophilic Mo sites, enabling dynamic charge redistribution and complementary catalytic behavior. Such a donor‐acceptor bridge effectively regulates intermediate adsorption/desorption and suppresses competing reaction pathways, thereby favoring the selective and reversible formation of Li 2 C 2 O 4 . Operando spectroscopic analysis confirms the preferential reversible Li 2 C 2 O 4 evolution during cycle, while density functional theory calculations reveal substantially reduced energy barriers for key reaction intermediates. Benefiting from the unique electronic environment and synergistic effects of asymmetric dual‐atom sites, the FeMoCN catalyst delivers outstanding electrochemical performance.

papers.title: Accelerating Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution via Interface‐To‐Surface Proton Transfer Relays on Ru‐RuO2−δ Heterostructure
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Ru has been investigated as a promissing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) catalyst in anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMWEs). However, its excessive oxophilicity blocks active sites and over‐structures interfacial water, limiting alkaline HER kinetics. In this work, we report a Ru‐RuO 2−δ heterostructure that overcomes these kinetic bottlenecks via an engineered interface‐to‐surface proton transfer relay. This architecture promotes a more flexible interfacial water network that facilitates Grotthuss‐type proton transport, coupled with facilitated hydrogen spillover from high‐affinity Ru clusters to low‐affinity RuO 2−δ surfaces. By decoupling proton delivery from surface binding, the Ru‐RuO 2−δ achieves an intrinsic activity 26‐fold higher than pristine Ru, requiring ultra‐low overpotentials of only 15 ± 4 and 165 ± 6 mV at 10 and 1000 mA cm −2 , respectively. Notably, the catalyst demonstrates long‐term durability under high‐current‐density operation (> 470 h at 1 A cm −2 ) with a degradation rate 2,000‐fold lower than commercial Pt/C. In a practical AEMWE, it delivers 1 A cm −2 at a cell voltage of 1.67 ± 0.02 V (45.1 ± 0.5 kWh kg H2 −1 ), meeting the U.S. DOE energy‐consumption target. Beyond providing a high‐performance alternative to platinum, this work introduces a design principle for accelerating electrocatalytic kinetics through the engineering of interface‐to‐surface transport relays.

papers.title: Mo2C‐Mediated Surface Reconstruction in MoNi4@Mo2C Heterostructure for Efficient Electrocatalytic Urea Oxidation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Replacing the oxygen evolution reaction with the urea oxidation reaction (UOR) offers an energy‐saving route for H 2 production, yet rational regulation of surface reconstruction in Ni‐based UOR electrocatalysts remains challenging. Herein, we report a MoNi 4 @Mo 2 C heterostructure and demonstrate its Mo 2 C‐mediated reconstruction of surface Ni species toward NiOOH‐containing active species during UOR. As a result, MoNi 4 @Mo 2 C requires only 1.26 V vs. RHE to reach 10 mA cm −2 and delivers 199.3 mA cm −2 at 1.30 V vs. RHE, outperforming MoNi 4 , Mo 2 C, and most reported Ni‐based UOR electrocatalysts. Electrochemical measurements reveal the dynamic generation, consumption, and regeneration of high‐valent Ni species during UOR. In situ Raman spectroscopy confirms the potential‐dependent formation of NiOOH‐containing active species, while electrochemical impedance measurements demonstrate accelerated charge‐transfer kinetics. When assembled in a two‐electrode electrolyzer, MoNi 4 @Mo 2 C||Pt/C delivers 112.3 mA cm −2 at 1.40 V and lowers the cell voltage by 210 mV at 100 mA cm −2 relative to conventional water electrolysis. This work highlights the importance of Mo 2 C‐mediated surface reconstruction in regulating active Ni species for UOR and offers insights into the rational design of Ni–Mo‐based heterostructures for efficient urea electrolysis.

papers.title: Organic Ligand‐Functionalized CoN2‐C‐N2Ni Dual‐Atom for Tailored Proton and Non‐Proton Transfer in Hydrogen Evolution and Triiodide Reduction
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Regulating the sustained transport and local concentration of reactive intermediates is essential for accelerating kinetics; however, constructing effective pathways for transferring both protonic and non‐protonic intermediates remains challenging. Herein, we present organic ligand‐functionalized interfacial engineering by anchoring trimesic acid (TMA) to MXene‐supported Co/Ni dual‐atom sites (TMA‐CoNi DA ‐MXene) to establish carboxyl‐mediated proton and non‐proton transport channels. By leveraging continuous π–π stacking and deprotonated ─COO − groups in aromatic frameworks, TMA‐CoNi DA ‐MXene facilitated the capture and delivery of I * /H * intermediates toward Co/Ni dual active sites, while also mitigating localized excessive accumulation of I * /H * . By exploiting the expanded interlayer spacing, stabilized CoN 2 ‐C‐N 2 Ni centers, and tailored transport pathways, TMA‐CoNi DA ‐MXene achieved a photoconversion efficiency of 8.62% as a counter electrode in iodine‐based solar cells and attained 10 mA cm −2 with an overpotential of only 71 mV in the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). This work provides insightful perspectives on integrating carboxylated organic ligands to jointly transfer protonic and non‐protonic intermediates and offers new approaches for organic–inorganic interfacial design in other complex systems.

papers.title: Engineering Ni0/δ+‐Coσ+ Pairs to Facilitate Interfacial Water Restructuring and Promote Volmer‐Heyrovsky‐Dominated Hydrogen Evolution
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal phosphide alloy materials exhibit application potential in alkaline water electrolysis for green hydrogen production. However, interfacial H 2 O structure, along with protons kinetic behavior at the interface in hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) remain elusive. Herein, we report a site‐substitution‐electronic modulation strategy to construct P‐bridged Ni 0/δ+ ‐Co σ+ pairs in Ni mesh (NM) supported NiCoP (NiCoP‐NM), wherein Co substitution at Ni sites modulates the electronic structure and generates an electron‐rich Ni center. The experiment and theoretical studies reveal that the Ni 0/δ+ ‐Co σ+ pairs redistribute the electron spin orientation at Ni sites, strengthening H* binding, and increasing surface H* coverage, which accelerates Heyrovsky kinetics by facilitating H 2 release. Additional, Ni 0/δ+ ‐Co σ+ pairs reorganize the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network and increase K + concentration in closest ion plane, leading to stronger H 2 O adsorption (−1.52 vs. −0.96 eV on NiP‐NM) and a lower H 2 O dissociation barrier (1.59 vs. 1.64 eV on NiP‐NM), thereby facilitating Volmer kinetics via boosting H 2 O activation. Consequently, NiCoP‐NM achieves outstanding HER performance with an overpotential of only 86.75 mV at 100 mA cm −2 , along with stability over 1000 h. This work offers a new strategy for designing metal phosphide alloys that tailor interfacial water structure and proton dynamics for advanced electrosynthesis.

papers.title: Coordination‐Based Regulation of Integrated Photoanodes for Boosted Water Oxidation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting for hydrogen evolution has been deemed a promising approach for solving the world's sustainable energy‐related and environmental challenges. However, poor charge separation in semiconductor photoelectrodes is the major challenge to overall solar energy conversion efficiencies. Moreover, n‐type semiconductors as photoanodes exhibit sluggish water oxidation kinetics. Coordination‐based regulation between semiconductors and cocatalysts as a form of interface optimization in integrated photoanodes has been proved an effective strategy to optimize charge transfer and water oxidation processes. Herein, recent critical headway on improving the efficiency of semiconductor‐based photoanodes for water oxidation via coordination‐based regulation is reviewed. In particular, this review aims to clarify how coordination‐based regulation achieves performance enhancement through the joint modulation of surface states and spin‐electronic states. The mechanism of coordination‐based regulation in integrated photoanodes on charge transfer and water oxidation kinetics prioritization scheme is demonstrated in detail. These benefits of coordination‐based regulation for efficient and stable water splitting devices will show huge advantages in the future.

papers.title: Substoichiometric [4+3] Strategy for Constructing Subvalent COFs with Acrylonitrile Unit Toward Solar‐Driven H 2 O 2 Production from Seawater
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid charge carrier recombination and limited active site availability remain major challenges for photocatalytic production of H 2 O 2 in water, particularly in seawater. Herein, we propose a substoichiometric [4+3] strategy to construct a subvalent covalent organic framework (TAQ‐COF) functionalized with acrylonitrile and benzoxadiazole moieties and the off‐stoichiometry of the polymerization reaction preserves two unreacted aldehyde groups per node. The resulting TAQ‐COF exhibits outstanding visible‐light‐driven H 2 O 2 production in pure water without any sacrificial agent, retains approximately 93% of its activity in seawater, and demonstrates excellent recyclability and antibacterial performance. Both theoretical and experimental evidence demonstrate that the enhanced local electron density surrounding the benzoxadiazole moieties in TAQ‐COF creates a favorable microenvironment for the proton‐coupled reduction of O 2 . Owing to its strong electron‐withdrawing effect and conjugated structure, the acrylonitrile unit markedly extends the lifetime of photogenerated charge carriers from 1.50 to 17.94 ns. Moreover, the enhanced surface hydrophilicity of TAQ‐COF sample promotes interfacial water enrichment, thereby favoring the proton‐coupled oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). The synergy of these features endows TAQ‐COF with outstanding catalytic activity in the two‐electron ORR pathway. This work demonstrates that synergistic functionalization with acrylonitrile units in a substoichiometric COF yields robust photocatalysts.

papers.title: Dual‐Site Engineering of a Noble‐Metal‐Free Z‐Scheme Heterojunction for Radical‐Kinetics‐Steered Selective C–C Coupling
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective photocatalytic C─C homocoupling of amines remains challenging due to uncontrollable radical kinetics and over‐oxidation. Herein, we construct a noble‐metal‐free Z‐scheme Cr‐TiO 2 @N‐C/CdS heterojunction photocatalyst that decouples thermodynamic and kinetic control through a dual‐site strategy. The incorporation of N‐doped carbon buffer layer not only resolves the intrinsic work function mismatch between Cr‐TiO 2 and CdS for efficient Z‐scheme charge transfer, but also facilitates rational control over the sequential arrangement of interfaces, thereby precisely regulating the coupling sites. Thermodynamically, Cr‐induced impurity levels near the valence band edge of TiO 2 moderate hole oxidation potential, preventing over‐oxidation of benzylamine. Kinetically, at the CdS surface, strong electronic interactions between surface three‐coordinated Cd atoms and the Ph( • CH)NH 2 radical impede further oxidation to imine, maintaining a high local radical concentration and exclusively driving C─C coupling. Consequently, under blue light, this heterojunction selectively converts benzylamine to the corresponding diamine (∼80% selectivity and an apparent quantum yield of 2.78%) with simultaneous high‐rate hydrogen evolution through a concerted proton‐coupled electron transfer pathway. This selectivity is broadly applicable to other benzylamine derivatives and benzyl alcohol systems. This work demonstrates that coordinated regulation of redox and surface reaction sites provides a robust strategy for achieving controllable radical dynamics and selective C─C bond synthesis.

papers.title: Engineering Acidic CO 2 Electroreduction for Efficient and Durable Formic Acid Production
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical synthesis of formic acid (HCOOH) via the carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) in acidic electrolytes can circumvent the severe CO 2 loss in alkaline and neutral conditions. However, simultaneously attaining high HCOOH production efficiency and durable long‐term operation in acidic CO 2 RR remains a critical bottleneck impeding the technology's practical deployment. Herein, we first discuss the core challenges faced by acidic CO 2 RR to HCOOH, most notably the competing hydrogen evolution reaction, serious catalyst deactivation, and the inherent trade‐off between product selectivity and carbon utilization efficiency. Then, key strategies to improve CO 2 to HCOOH conversion efficiency are systematically summarized, with a focus on stabilization of key reaction intermediates and rational engineering of the catalytic microenvironment. Additionally, effective approaches to enhance catalyst durability, as well as the design of advanced electrolyzer configurations tailored for acidic CO 2 RR systems, are elaborated. We end the review by outlining the existing challenges and future directions for accelerating the industrialization of acidic CO 2 RR to HCOOH.

papers.title: How the Porous Transport Layer Dictates Membrane Electrode Assembly Performance of IrO 2 Catalysts
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Reducing the use of precious metals is essential for the commercialization of proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE). The Schottky contact formed between the catalyst layer and Ti porous transport layer (PTL) at the anode significantly degrades cell performance and necessitates high Ir loading or Pt coating. IrO 2 catalysts with various crystallite sizes (1.7‒11.0 nm) were synthesized, and their membrane electrode assembly (MEA) performance was evaluated at a low Ir loading of 0.3 mg Ir cm −2 using Pt‐coated Ti PTL and bare Ti PTL. The MEA performance exhibited opposite trends depending on the type of PTL, primarily due to variation in the work function, which is determined by the surface oxygen configuration of the IrO 2 catalyst. Smaller crystallites exhibited a larger work function, resulting in a greater performance discrepancy between the two PTL types. To overcome the suboptimal performance of IrO 2 , we utilized the crystalline 7.1 nm‐sized IrO 2 as an electron pathway and deposited highly active amorphous IrO x on its surface. This mixed‐phase Ir oxide exhibited good cell performance and durability even with a bare Ti PTL. This study highlights that the Schottky contact problem of IrO 2 catalysts can be overcome through surface engineering, enabling low Ir use for PEMWE.

papers.title: Rational Construction of Multicomponent Electrocatalyst via Cluster‐Nanoparticle Synergy for Enhanced Hydrogen Production Coupled With Hydrazine Oxidation at Large Current Densities
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrazine‐assisted water electrolysis enables low‐energy‐consumption hydrogen production while simultaneously facilitating the harmless treatment of hydrazine‐containing pollutants. Herein, a hydrothermal and air‐annealing strategy was employed to simultaneously anchor Ru nanoclusters and Pt nanoparticles on NiO nanowires, thereby constructing a bifunctional Pt‐Ru/NiO catalyst with synergistic dual‐sites for the hydrazine oxidation reaction (HzOR) and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). This study reveals that the incorporation of Pt and Ru effectively tailors the electronic configuration, optimizing the free energy of hydrogen adsorption/desorption and N 2 H 4 dehydrogenation kinetics, thus endowing the catalyst with outstanding HER and HzOR electrocatalytic activity. To attain the current density of 1000 mA cm − 2 , Pt‐Ru/NiO merely requires working potentials of 0.158 V for HER and 0.157 V for HzOR, respectively. Impressively, with Pt‐Ru/NiO functioning as cathode and anode, the assembled full hydrazine electrolyzer yields 200 mA cm − 2 at an extremely low cell voltage of just 0.057 V, with stable operation sustained for more than 100 h. This work provides a design framework for cluster‐particle dual‐site synergistic systems and offers a new pathway for hydrazine‐assisted high‐efficiency electrolytic hydrogen production technology.

papers.title: Bridging the Gap Between Photocatalytic Water Oxidation Half‐Reaction and Stoichiometric Pure Water Splitting Over Ta3N5 via Cocatalyst Engineering
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite significant progress in photocatalytic half‐reactions and photoelectrochemical water oxidation, achieving stable photocatalytic pure water splitting over Ta 3 N 5 remains a long‐standing challenge. Herein, the incompatibility of cocatalysts between alkaline photocatalytic water oxidation systems and pure water splitting is identified as a critical bottleneck, leading to serious N 2 generation through photocorrosion. To address this challenge, a highly dispersed RuCoO x cocatalyst is developed via a multi‐step incipient wetness impregnation strategy. The optimized Pt@Cr 2 O 3 /Ta 3 N 5 /RuCoO x achieves stoichiometric pure water splitting with an apparent quantum yield of 0.72% at 420 nm, representing the highest value reported for Ta‐based nitride/oxynitride photocatalysts to date. Mechanistic studies reveal that an enhanced interfacial electric field facilitates hole extraction, while a reduced formation barrier of key intermediates accelerates surface reaction kinetics, thereby overcoming the long‐standing bottleneck in photocatalytic pure water splitting over Ta 3 N 5 . This work establishes cocatalyst compatibility as a key design consideration for stable photocatalytic pure water splitting and provides mechanistic insight for the rational design of advanced nitride and oxynitride photocatalysts.

papers.title: Engineering Carbon Cloth‐Catalyst Interfaces for Pt‐Free Hydrogen Evolution Across the Full pH Spectrum
papers.abstract: The development of Pt-free electrocatalysts is critical for reducing the cost of hydrogen production through the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Although extensive efforts have focused on improving the intrinsic activity of earth-abundant catalysts, the role of the catalyst-support interface remains comparatively underexplored. Carbon cloth (CC) has emerged as an attractive electrode platform owing to its electrical conductivity, hierarchical porosity, mechanical flexibility, chemical stability, and ability to facilitate efficient charge and mass transport. Although CC is generally not the primary HER active phase, it can strongly influence electrode-level performance by regulating interfacial electron transfer, catalyst anchoring, active-site accessibility, wettability, hydrogen bubble release, and long-term durability. This review critically analyzes the interfacial synergy between CC and Pt-free transition-metal-based catalysts, including Co-, Ni-, Fe-, Cu-, Mo-, and W-based systems, with and without heteroatom or anion modification involving N, P, and S species. The HER activity and stability of these systems are evaluated under acidic, alkaline, neutral, and pH-universal conditions. A particular emphasis is placed on how catalyst-support interactions, synthesis strategies, surface chemistry, structural features, and mass-transport behavior collectively determine electrochemical performance. Finally, current challenges and future opportunities are discussed, including mechanistic understanding, operando characterization, high-current-density operation, long-term durability, scalable fabrication, and practical electrolyzer integration.

papers.title: Accelerated Discovery of Earth‐Abundant Oxygen Evolution Catalysts Through Surface‐Informed Active Learning
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of efficient electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a challenge in alkaline water electrolysis. Discovering optimal compositions for complex multi‐element electrocatalysts is time‐intensive and resource‐consuming due to the vast compositional space. Here, we propose a hybrid computational strategy that integrates active learning (AL)‐assisted screening with density functional theory (DFT) calculations to accelerate the development of multielement alloy electrocatalysts. Our approach employs 15 cycles of active learning, with 20 NiCoFe (NCF) surface configurations evaluated per cycle, totaling 300 DFT calculations. To minimize computational cost, we utilized scaling relationships and calculated only *O and *OH adsorption energies, while the AL featurization incorporated surface configuration information. This methodology filtered the compositional space of Ni x Co y Fe 100‐x‐y alloys and identified the optimal composition of Ni 55 Co 10 Fe 35 . Experimental validation demonstrated that the optimized NCF exhibits accelerated OER kinetics and practical activity, as evidenced by a low Tafel slope of 43.07 mV dec −1 while maintaining 98.68% of its initial performance over 24 h at 10 mA cm −2 . This study demonstrates the effectiveness of the hybrid AL‐DFT strategy for resource‐efficient composition screening within the NiCoFe ternary alloy system and highlights its potential for application to other multicomponent catalyst systems following appropriate system‐specific model development and validation.

papers.title: Cluster‐Scale MoOx‐IrO2 Heterointerfaces Steer Dual‐Site Coupling and Interfacial Water Dynamics for Fast and Durable Oxygen Evolution
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) are central to renewable‐powered green hydrogen production. As the benchmark electrocatalyst for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), conventional single‐phase IrO 2 is constrained by linear scaling relations among oxygenated intermediates, compounded by severe mass‐transport limitations and poorly regulated interfacial water structures. Here, we design a Turing‐type MoO x ‐IrO 2 heterostructure with strongly coupled cluster‐scale interfaces, which enables dual‐function Ir‐Mo synergy that breaks fundamental kinetic limitations and optimizes interfacial water structures. At the reaction pathway level, Brønsted‐acidic MoO x clusters promote water dissociation to generate reactive Mo─OH* intermediates, triggering radical coupling with adjacent Ir─O* species to form OOH* and thus circumventing the linear scaling relation. At the interfacial microenvironment level, MoO x reorganizes the rigid hydrogen‐bonding networks and increases the population of free H 2 O species, effectively alleviating concentration overpotentials under high‐current‐density operation. When integrated into a practical 25 cm 2 membrane electrode assembly, this catalyst delivers a PEMWE cell voltage of 1.71 V at 3 A cm −2 and an ultralow degradation rate of ∼9.5 µV h −1 over 1000 h, with a total platinum‐group‐metal loading of merely 0.5 mg cm −2 across both electrodes. Our dual‐modulation strategy establishes a transformative paradigm for developing low‐iridium and durable OER electrocatalysts toward practical green hydrogen production.

papers.title: Interfacial Hydrogen Spillover in Partially Alloyed PdNi Electrocatalysts for Hydrogen Evolution
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen spillover can decouple elementary steps in the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet conventional bimetallic catalysts often suffer from discontinuous interfaces that block spillover pathways. Herein, an interfacial hydrogen spillover mechanism is engineered in a Pd–PdNi–Ni catalyst via a partial interface alloying strategy for pH‐universal hydrogen evolution. The graded PdNi interface serves as a recombination sink integrating two synergistic pathways: primary spillover, in which strongly adsorbed H* generated on Ni spontaneously migrates across the interface, and secondary spillover, in which H* produced on Pd also diffuses to the same interfacial sites. The dual spillover is driven by a favorable hydrogen intermediate gradient resulting from Ni‐to‐Pd electron transfer and an optimized d‐band center. The optimal catalyst delivers ultralow overpotentials of 60 mV (alkaline) and 37 mV (acidic) at 10 mA cm −2 , with robust durability, and the corresponding anion exchange membrane electrolyzer exhibits 1.73 V at 0.5 A cm −2 and 452 h stability in simulated seawater. Operando Raman spectroscopy detects Pd–H and Ni–H vibrations, providing direct evidence for hydrogen migration from both domains to the interface, and theoretical calculations confirm the electronic origin and spillover pathways. This work demonstrates a rational design for high‐performance HER catalysts by harnessing dual hydrogen spillover.

papers.title: From Atoms to Reactors: A Critical Review of a Decade of Machine Learning in Heterogeneous Catalysis (2017–2026)
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This critical review traces the evolution of machine learning (ML) across the full value chain of heterogeneous catalysis over 2017–2026, from catalyst discovery to reactor and process design, and across the principal reaction families (CO 2 reduction, water splitting, nitrogen chemistry, zeolite‐catalyzed transformations). Each stage is evaluated against four criteria — data foundation, method maturity, experimental validation and deployment readiness — through a structured capability scorecard. Digitalization has advanced from the top of the length scale downward: prediction of adsorption energies and atomistic potential‐energy surfaces is now mature, with errors of tens of meV relative to the reference DFT calculations and accelerations of three orders of magnitude over DFT, yet experimentally validated catalyst improvements remain rare. The most significant advance is the closed‐loop autonomous laboratory coupling Bayesian optimization, automated synthesis and high‐throughput testing. Large language models have begun to add a reasoning and orchestration layer, while kinetics, reactor and process design remain the least digitalized stages. We argue that the field's next decade of impact will be decided not by more accurate atomic‐scale prediction but by carrying ML into experimental validation and the reactor‐and‐process scale, where catalysis is hardest to industrialize and where data‐driven methods are weakest.

papers.title: Reusable and Robust Hydrogel With Dynamic Sacrificial S─S Bonds: In Situ Construction of an Integrated SEI/Hydrogel Interface for Highly Stable Zn–I 2 Batteries
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The trade‐off among mechanical strength, ionic conductivity, and interfacial stability remains a core challenge for high‐performance hydrogel interfacial layers. Herein, an integrated SEI/polyurea–polyurethane hydrogel (PUMA) interface was constructed on the Zn anode via in situ gelation coupled with interfacial electrochemical reduction. Polyurea–polyurethane hard segments containing octuple H‐bonds, Zn 2+ coordination bonds, and dynamic S─S bonds reinforce PUMA through multi‐level energy dissipation and suppress side reactions by regulating interfacial water. Polyanionic soft segments rich in carboxyl and sulfonic acid groups construct low‐barrier, ion‐selective pathways, optimizing Zn 2+ transport and deposition by solvation regulation and mitigation of concentration polarization. Crucially, interfacial sacrificial S─S bonds undergo cleavage during electrochemical reduction, generating an integrated SEI/PUMA interface with enhanced interfacial stability. The dynamic polyanionic network also blocks polyiodide shuttling and enables thermal reprocessing. Consequently, PUMA@Zn achieves a Zn 2+ transference number of 0.79 and symmetric cell cycling for 5080 h (1 mA cm −2 and 0.5 mAh cm −2 ). PUMA@Zn//I 2 cells retain 88% capacity after 43 000 cycles at 4 A g −1 and operate for over 11 000 cycles even at high iodine loading (16.58 mg cm −2 ). This strategy provides a novel pathway to achieve robust, ion‐conductivity, and chemically bonded hydrogel–metal interfaces for high‐performance aqueous batteries.

papers.title: Pd Embedded in 1T‐Rich MoS 2 With Island‐Sea Confinement for C 2 ‐Selective Ethanol Electrooxidation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Direct ethanol fuel cells (DEFCs) are hampered by sluggish C─C bond cleavage and CO poisoning during ethanol electrooxidation on Pd catalysts. Selective oxidation to acetate through the C 2 pathway circumvents CO formation, yet achieving near‐exclusive C 2 selectivity remains challenging. Herein, we report a nitrogen‐doping‐induced expansion strategy that converts bulk 2H‐MoS 2 into a metastable 1T‐rich MoS 2‐x support (NTMS x ) with enlarged interlayer spacing and abundant sulfur vacancies. Conductive 1T domains preferentially anchor Pd nanoparticles, creating an “island‐sea” architecture that fosters pronounced electronic metal‐support interaction (EMSI). Electron transfer from NTMS x to Pd generates electron‐rich Pd sites that weaken CO adsorption, while sulfur vacancies enhance hydroxyl adsorption. These synergistic effects steer ethanol electrooxidation toward the C 2 ‐4e pathway and suppress CO formation. DFT calculations confirm favorable energetics for the C 2 pathway on Pd/NTMS x . The catalyst delivers a high current density and 95.7% Faradaic efficiency for acetate of high added value, with no detectable CO intermediates and outstanding durability. In DEFCs, it achieves a maximum power density of 0.68 W cm −2 and operates stably for over 500 h. This work establishes confined interfacial anchoring on phase‐engineered metal dichalcogenides as a rational design principle for achieving high pathway selectivity in multielectron electrocatalysis.

papers.title: 2D Borophene Oxide Substrate for C 2+ Products Synthesis via CO 2 Electroreduction at Industrial Current Densities
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The industrialization of electrochemical CO 2 reduction reaction for multi‐carbon products synthesis is limited by HER competition, sluggish C─C coupling kinetics, and carbonate deposition. Through rational computational screening, we identify β ‐rhombohedral borophene oxide ( β ‐rh. BO) as an ideal two‐dimensional substrate to simultaneously overcome these bottlenecks. Evaluated in a flow cell with 1 M KOH electrolyte, the β ‐rh. BO‐supported Cu (BO–Cu) demonstrates outstanding performance across an industrially relevant current density range of −700 to −1500 mA cm −2 , achieving a peak C 2+ Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 85.9% and a partial current density exceeding −1082 mA cm −2 . Mechanistic studies reveal that β ‐rh. BO serves a role beyond an electron donor. Specifically, it redistributes hydrated K + and alters the interfacial water structure, which not only suppresses HER by diverting proton transfer toward *CO hydrogenation rather than H 2 evolution, but also enables the transformation of symmetric C─C coupling to asymmetric C─C coupling via modulating the charge distribution of intermediates. Furthermore, the introduction of β ‐rh. BO drastically reduces carbonate deposition. This work presents a novel multifunctional substrate that synergistically modulates the electronic structure, tailors interfacial water structure, and suppresses carbonate deposition, offering a new paradigm for the design of electrocatalysts for industrial CO 2 RR applications.

papers.title: Interfacial Charge Modulation of Covalent Metal–Organic Frameworks for Efficient H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical H 2 O 2 synthesis through the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction offers a sustainable alternative to the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. Crystalline porous frameworks are attractive for this route because of their structural precision, yet poor electrolyte wetting and limited electrochemical accessibility often restrict their practical performance. Here, we report an interfacial charge‐modulation strategy that transforms covalent metal–organic frameworks into highly wetted and electrochemically accessible catalytic interfaces. By incorporating cationic ethidium bromide units into a trinuclear copper‐pyrazolate framework, we construct EB‐Cu 3 ‐COF featuring enlarged interlayer spacing, enhanced interfacial charge transfer, and optimized *OOH intermediate adsorption. Consequently, EB‐Cu 3 ‐COF achieves up to 99% H 2 O 2 selectivity and a flow‐cell production rate of 39 420 mmol·g cat −1 ·h −1 , ranking among the best‐performing non‐pyrolyzed porous organic electrocatalysts reported to date. This work establishes interfacial charge‐modulation as a design principle for translating crystalline structural precision into electrochemically active interfaces.

papers.title: Understanding the Instability Origin for Design of Robust Pure RuO2 Anode Catalyst in PEM Water Electrolysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Ruthenium dioxide (RuO2) shows great promise as an acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalyst in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), yet its insufficient stability─often attributed to Ru overoxidation─actually has a hidden cause. Herein, we show that the true culprit is instead residual chloride impurities inherited from the most commonly used RuCl3 precursor. Owing to strong Ru–Cl coordination, substantial chlorine residues are trapped in the RuO2 lattice during conventional synthesis; during electrolysis, they gradually leach out, dramatically accelerating Ru dissolution and lattice oxygen loss and triggering structural collapse. Guided by this insight, we developed a small-molecule-assisted synthesis that yields Cl-free RuO2. The resulting catalyst preserves exceptional structural integrity, sustains its initial activity through 80,000 accelerated degradation cycles, and delivers stable PEMWE operation at 500 mA cm–2 for 500 h, outperforming all reported single RuO2 catalysts and rivaling even the best doped or composite Ru-based catalysts. Our findings resolve a long-standing paradox in RuO2 catalysis and establish chloride elimination as a critical design principle for durable oxide electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Radical–Electrochemical Coupling Enables Amination of Methane
papers.abstract: Abstract The selective functionalization of methane under ambient conditions is widely regarded as a holy grail in chemistry, yet remains fundamentally limited not only by the inertness of the C–H bond but also by the transient nature of highly reactive intermediates. Short-lived species are often difficult to preserve and utilize prior to productive coupling, constraining accessible reaction pathways and product selectivity. Here, we establish a reaction framework based on in situ interfacial interception of reactive radicals, enabling the temporal coordination between radical lifetime and subsequent reaction processes. Plasma generates short-lived methyl radicals in immediate proximity to a gas–electrode interface, allowing their direct delivery and capture at the catalytic surface, while the electrochemical interface independently converts ammonia into surface-bound amino intermediates. Their coupling enables selective C–N bond formation. This spatially and temporally coordinated process allows highly reactive radical species to be synchronized with interfacial reaction steps, facilitating their productive utilization. Guided by density functional theory, we identify a nickel–cobalt layered double hydroxide catalyst that promotes interfacial coupling between *CH3 and *NH2 intermediates. The optimized system achieves a Faradaic efficiency of 54% for methylamine at 10 mA cm–2, with a productivity of 201 μmol cm–2 h–1 under ambient conditions. Beyond methane amination, this work demonstrates that coordinating the lifetime and transformation of reactive intermediates provides a generalizable strategy for catalytic control, offering new opportunities for the activation and selective transformation of inert molecules.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights of Jahn–Teller Effect Suppression in High-Entropy Prussian Blue Analogue Cathodes
papers.abstract: Abstract The Jahn–Teller (J-T) effect, as discovered by Hermann Jahn and Edward Teller in 1937, often causes lattice distortion and structural instability in Mn-based battery materials. Recent studies suggest that high-entropy design may help suppress J-T distortion, yet the underlying mechanism remains largely elusive due to their compositional complexity and structural disorder. Herein, using a Mn-based Prussian blue analogue as a case study, we employed a machine learning interatomic potential combined with synchrotron extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy (EXAFS) to elucidate the fundamental mechanism of the J-T suppression in high-entropy materials. Unexpectedly, EXAFS spectra reveal the absence of the typical J-T Mn–N bond-length splitting in our high-entropy Prussian blue analogue sample, but instead a broader Mn–N bond-length distribution. Machine learning-assisted calculations demonstrate the [MnN6] octahedra exhibit randomly oriented distortions along x-, y-, and z-axes in high-entropy lattices, resulting in the local distortion averaging out at the macroscopic scale. Further analysis of the local Mn coordination environment reveals that the high-entropy configuration enhances d-electron delocalization and reduces the energy splitting between Mn dx2–y2 and dz2 orbitals. This allows two structurally and electronically distinct distortion modes to coexist within the lattice, which disrupts long-range cooperative J-T order. Strikingly, the ultralong cycling stability of high-entropy K0.46[Mn0.21Co0.19Ni0.21Cu0.20Zn0.19][Fe(CN)6]0.98·1.69H2O is experimentally demonstrated, achieving 91.0% capacity retention over 50,000 cycles for aqueous ammonium-ion storage, which surpasses all of the Mn-based rechargeable batteries to date. Our study uncovers the microscopic mechanism of J-T suppression in high-entropy materials and provides an effective strategy for designing durable high-entropy battery electrodes.

papers.title: Operando Time-Resolved Spectroelectrochemical Microscopy Reveals Distinct Electron Depletion Pathways in Electrocatalysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Understanding electrocatalysis requires direct knowledge of how charge carriers are distributed and consumed at active sites under the operating conditions. However, the spatiotemporal dynamics of injected electrons in working catalysts remain largely inaccessible, hindering a mechanistic understanding of catalytic heterogeneity. Here, we develop an operando time-resolved spectroelectrochemical microscopy that enables direct and quantitative mapping of electron density with microsecond temporal resolution and micrometer spatial resolution. Using monolayer MoS2 as a model system, we directly visualize the spatial redistribution and depletion of electrochemically injected electrons during the hydrogen evolution reaction. We observe pronounced site-specific electron depletion that correlates with catalytic activity and further identify two distinct mechanisms governing charge loss: reaction-limited depletion at highly active sites, including edges and Pt-functionalized sites, and injection-limited depletion in bilayer regions. These results establish a quantitative link between local charge carrier dynamics and catalytic activity and provide a general framework for probing nanoscale carrier dynamics in electrocatalysts.
